**4. Maintenance Request Resolution Policy**

The Chairman raised the issue of the increasing number of maintenance requests and the need for a clear, standardised procedure for resolving them. Several members expressed concerns about the varying time taken to address complaints, with some requests pending for over two weeks.

After detailed deliberation, the committee unanimously agreed to adopt a formal policy for resolution of maintenance requests. The policy is as follows:

**Resolution:** In the minutes of the Managing Committee dated 2023-03-15, Silverline Cooperative Housing Society recorded that the maintenance_request_resolution_policy for non-emergency requests is standard_resolution_time_for_non_emergency_requests_is_7_working_days. Record status: current. This policy is applicable to all non-emergency maintenance requests received from members, including but not limited to plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and civil repairs. Emergency requests, such as water leakage, electrical short-circuits, and lift breakdowns, will continue to be addressed on an urgent basis, typically within 24 hours.

The policy will be displayed on the notice board and communicated to all members via the society WhatsApp group. A copy of the policy will also be attached to the next maintenance bill.

**Decision No. 2023/03/03:** The Maintenance Request Resolution Policy as stated above is adopted and shall be effective immediately for all new and pending non-emergency requests.

The Joint Secretary presented a summary of maintenance requests received during the period 1 February 2023 to 14 March 2023.

| Month | Total Requests | Resolved | Pending | Emergency Requests |

- **Lift door sensor issue:** The request was received on 12 March 2023. The lift maintenance company was called and the issue was resolved on the same day. This was treated as an emergency request.

The committee noted that with the adoption of the new policy, all pending non-emergency requests will be tracked against the 7-working-day timeline. The Joint Secretary will maintain a register of all requests and update the status on a weekly basis.

**8. Authorisation Limit for Maintenance Expenses**

The Secretary, Ms. Anjali Deshpande, raised a matter regarding the approval limit for maintenance expenses that she is authorised to sanction without prior committee approval. Currently, the limit is ₹10,000 per instance, which was set by a resolution in 2021. In light of the rising costs of repairs and the need to attend to urgent maintenance without delay, she proposed that the limit be revised.

The committee discussed the matter at length. Some members expressed concern that increasing the limit would reduce the committee’s oversight of expenditure. However, it was noted that the Secretary is required to report all such expenses at the next committee meeting, and that the current limit was proving insufficient for common repair works, such as plumbing and electrical jobs, which often cost more than ₹10,000.

After discussion, the committee agreed to raise the limit to ₹15,000 per instance. It was clarified that this limit applies only to maintenance expenses and does not cover new works, capital purchases, or any expenditure that has been separately budgeted. Any expense exceeding this limit must be brought to the committee for prior approval.

The Managing Committee resolution dated 2023-06-20 states that Anjali Deshpande's authorized_approval_limit_for_maintenance_expenses is 15000 INR. Record status: current. This limit is currently in effect and will be reviewed at the end of the financial year, or earlier if the need arises.

**Decision No. 2023/03/05:** The approval limit for maintenance expenses that can be sanctioned by the Secretary, Ms. Anjali Deshpande, without prior committee approval, is revised from ₹10,000 to ₹15,000 per instance. The Chairman placed before the committee the two quotations received for the basement waterproofing work, as per the discussions held in the previous meeting.

- **Aqua Shield Waterproofers:** ₹1,72,500. Scope includes crack filling with epoxy, one coat of acrylic waterproofing paint on walls, and one coat of cement-based coating on the floor. Work to be completed within 15 days. Warranty for 1 year.

The committee discussed the two quotations in detail. Mr. Anand Joshi pointed out that although Aqua Shield's quotation is lower, their scope of work is less comprehensive, particularly in respect of the treatment of the walls. The parking basement has had persistent seepage issues and water logging during the monsoon, and the committee felt that the quality of material and the longer warranty offered by Sunrise Maintenance Services would be more beneficial in the long run.

Mrs. Sunita Deshpande noted that Sunrise Maintenance Services had earlier completed the waterproofing of the overhead tank in 2021 and the work was found to be satisfactory. She also mentioned that the company's representative was available today to answer any questions.
Mr. Kulkarni drew the attention of the committee to a few items that were expected to be significantly higher than in the previous year. The electricity tariff had been revised by the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission with effect from 1 April 2023, and the society's consumption had also gone up because of the additional pumping required during the summer months. He proposed a provision of ₹4,20,000 under this head, as against ₹3,85,000 spent in the previous year.

The committee noted that the overall expenditure was projected at ₹20,40,000, leaving a surplus of approximately ₹1,25,000, which would be transferred to the general reserve.

**Resolution No. MC/23-24/07: Approval of Expenses above ₹15,000**

*Resolved that, with immediate effect, no expenditure exceeding ₹15,000 in respect of a single item or a single work order shall be incurred by the Managing Committee of Silverline without the prior approval of the general body of the society. The Managing Committee resolution dated 2023-06-20 states that Managing Committee of Silverline approval_required_for_expenses_above_15000 is general_body_meeting_approval. Record status: current. The resolution was proposed by Mrs. Sunita Deshpande and seconded by Mr. Anand Joshi. It was passed unanimously.

The Chairman raised the issue of the increasing number of maintenance requests and the need for a clear, standardised procedure for resolving them. Several members expressed concerns about the varying time taken to address complaints, with some requests pending for over two weeks.

After detailed deliberation, the committee unanimously agreed to adopt a formal policy for resolution of maintenance requests. The policy is as follows:

**Resolution:** In the minutes of the Managing Committee dated 2023-03-15, Silverline Cooperative Housing Society recorded that the maintenance_request_resolution_policy for non-emergency requests is standard_resolution_time_for_non_emergency_requests_is_7_working_days. Emergency requests, such as water leakage, electrical short-circuits, and lift breakdowns, will continue to be addressed on an urgent basis, typically within 24 hours.

The policy will be displayed on the notice board and communicated to all members via the society WhatsApp group. A copy of the policy will also be attached to the next maintenance bill.

**8. Authorisation Limit for Maintenance Expenses**

The Secretary, Ms. Anjali Deshpande, raised a matter regarding the approval limit for maintenance expenses that she is authorised to sanction without prior committee approval. Currently, the limit is ₹10,000 per instance, which was set by a resolution in 2021. In light of the rising costs of repairs and the need to attend to urgent maintenance without delay, she proposed that the limit be revised.

The committee discussed the matter at length. Some members expressed concern that increasing the limit would reduce the committee’s oversight of expenditure. However, it was noted that the Secretary is required to report all such expenses at the next committee meeting, and that the current limit was proving insufficient for common repair works, such as plumbing and electrical jobs, which often cost more than ₹10,000.

After discussion, the committee agreed to raise the limit to ₹15,000 per instance. It was clarified that this limit applies only to maintenance expenses and does not cover new works, capital purchases, or any expenditure that has been separately budgeted. Any expense exceeding this limit must be brought to the committee for prior approval.

The Managing Committee resolution dated 2023-06-20 states that Anjali Deshpande's authorized_approval_limit_for_maintenance_expenses is 15000 INR. Record status: current. This limit is currently in effect and will be reviewed at the end of the financial year, or earlier if the need arises.

**Decision No. 2023/03/05:** The approval limit for maintenance expenses that can be sanctioned by the Secretary, Ms. Anjali Deshpande, without prior committee approval, is revised from ₹10,000 to ₹15,000 per instance. This resolution is effective immediately and supersedes the earlier resolution dated 12 March 2021.

- **Overhead water tank cleaning:** The last cleaning was done in January 2023. The next cleaning is scheduled for July 2023, and the contractor has been informed. The cost of ₹8,500 will be borne from the maintenance budget.  
- **Painting of staircases:** A quotation was received from a local contractor for ₹45,000 for painting the three staircases. The committee decided to obtain one more quotation before taking a decision.  
- **Installation of CCTV cameras:** The proposal to install additional CCTV cameras in the parking area and the entrance lobby was discussed. The estimated cost is ₹60,000. The committee decided to defer this to the next meeting, as the quotations are yet to be finalised.

Mr. Kulkarni drew the attention of the committee to a few items that were expected to be significantly higher than in the previous year. The electricity tariff had been revised by the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission with effect from 1 April 2023, and the society's consumption had also gone up because of the additional pumping required during the summer months. He proposed a provision of ₹4,20,000 under this head, as against ₹3,85,000 spent in the previous year.

The committee noted that the overall expenditure was projected at ₹20,40,000, leaving a surplus of approximately ₹1,25,000, which would be transferred to the general reserve.

After a detailed discussion, the committee approved the budget for the financial year 2023–24. It was decided that the monthly maintenance charges would remain unchanged at ₹3,200 per flat per month for the present year.

Mrs. Sunita Deshpande raised a question regarding the procedure to be followed for incurring expenditure on items that were not provided for in the approved budget, or where the actual expenditure was likely to exceed the budgeted provision. She pointed out that in the past, on a few occasions, the committee had directly approved payments for urgent repairs without any reference to the general body, and that this had led to some questions being raised by members at the annual general meeting.

The Chairman, Mr. Ramesh Kulkarni, stated that it would be prudent to lay down a clear policy in this regard. After discussion, the committee unanimously passed the following resolution:

**Resolution No. MC/23-24/07: Approval of Expenses above ₹15,000**

*Resolved that, with immediate effect, no expenditure exceeding ₹15,000 in respect of a single item or a single work order shall be incurred by the Managing Committee of Silverline without the prior approval of the general body of the society. The Managing Committee resolution dated 2023-06-20 states that Managing Committee of Silverline approval_required_for_expenses_above_15000 is general_body_meeting_approval. Record status: current. This policy shall be applicable to all heads of expenditure, including repairs, maintenance, purchases, and contracts, whether or not provision for the same exists in the approved annual budget. The Secretary shall place the proposal before the general body at its next meeting, with full details of the work or purchase, the quotations received, and the recommendation of the committee. In cases of an emergency, where delay would result in damage to the society's property or danger to the residents, the committee may incur the expenditure after obtaining telephonic or written approval from at least three committee members, and the matter shall be placed before the general body at its next meeting for ratification.*

The resolution was proposed by Mrs. Sunita Deshpande and seconded by Mr. Anand Joshi. It was passed unanimously.

Mr. Baburao Jadhav, who was present at the meeting, asked whether this rule would also apply to routine recurring payments such as the monthly salary of the staff or the electricity bill. The Chairman clarified that the resolution was intended to apply to lump-sum payments and individual works or purchases, and not to recurring monthly charges which were already provided for in the budget. This clarification was accepted by the committee and recorded in the minutes.

---

**7. Proposal for the Installation of a New Water Purification System in the Society Clubhouse**

The Secretary informed the committee that the existing water purifier in the clubhouse had become old and was frequently breaking down. The filter cartridges were also not easily available in the market. He said that he had received a complaint from the members using the clubhouse, and he had obtained quotations for a new purifier.

**CIRCULAR No. SL/2023/18**
**Date: 5th May 2023**

**Subject: General Maintenance Reminders & Notice of Managing Committee Meeting**

Dear Members,

This circular covers a few routine maintenance matters requiring your cooperation, along with the
notice for the next Managing Committee (M.C.) meeting.

**1. Monsoon Preparedness – Balcony & Terrace Drains**

With the monsoon expected by early June, we request all residents to check the drain openings in
their balconies, terraces, and window sills. Blocked drains during heavy rain can cause water
logging on upper floors and seepage into the flats below.

- Please clear any accumulated dry leaves, dust, or debris from the drain mesh.
- Do not throw any solid waste, cloth, or plastic into the drains.
- If you notice any crack in the drain pipe or the waterproofing near the balcony, please report it
  to the Maintenance Supervisor, Shri Suresh Patil, at the society office so that a repair can be
  scheduled before the rains.

**2. Lift Maintenance – Scheduled Downtime**

The annual maintenance contract for all four lifts is due. The service engineer from the lift
company, M/s. Otis Elevator Co., will carry out the maintenance on **Saturday, 13th May 2023** and
**Sunday, 14th May 2023**.

- **13/05/2023 (Saturday):** Lifts in Block A and Block B will be shut down from 10:00 a.m. to
  4:00 p.m. (one lift at a time, as far as possible).
- **14/05/2023 (Sunday):** Lifts in Block C and Block D will be shut down from 10:00 a.m. to
  4:00 p.m.

We will try to minimise the downtime. In case of an emergency during the shutdown, please contact
the watchman at the main gate, who has been instructed to assist.

**3. Parking – Visitor Parking Bay Discipline**

It has been observed that some visitor parking bays in the basement are being occupied by residents'
own vehicles for extended periods, sometimes overnight. This causes inconvenience to actual guests.

As per the society's parking rules (Bye-law 14), visitor parking bays are meant for short-term
parking of guests only (maximum 4 hours). Residents are requested to strictly adhere to this. From
**15th May 2023** onwards, the watchman has been instructed to note down the vehicle numbers of cars
parked in visitor bays beyond the permitted time, and a warning sticker will be placed on the
windshield. Repeat offenders will be issued a formal notice.

**4. Common Area Cleaning – New Schedule**

The cleaning contractor has revised the schedule for common area cleaning. The new schedule is
effective from **1st June 2023**:

| Day | Area |
|-----|------|
| Monday | Staircases & lift lobbies (all blocks) |
| Tuesday | Basement parking & ramps |
| Wednesday | Compound, garden paths & children's play area |
| Thursday | Terrace & service floors |
| Friday | Staircases & lift lobbies (all blocks) |
| Saturday | Basement parking & ramps (deep cleaning) |

The garbage collection from the chute will continue as before (twice daily – 8:00 a.m. and 8:00
p.m.).

**5. Notice of Managing Committee Meeting**

The next Managing Committee meeting will be held on:

**Date:** Saturday, 20th May 2023
**Time:** 6:00 p.m.
**Venue:** Society Office

**Agenda:**

1. Confirmation of minutes of the previous M.C. meeting.
2. Review of the election process for the new Managing Committee (as per Circular No. SL/2023/16).
3. Approval of the annual maintenance contract for lifts.
4. Discussion on the repair of the boundary wall near the rear gate (cracks noticed during the
   pre-monsoon inspection).
5. Any other matter with the permission of the Chairperson.

All M.C. members are requested to make it convenient to attend. Members of the society who wish to
bring up any issue may send a note to the Secretary at the office or by email to
secysl2023@example.com at least two days prior to the meeting, so that it can be included in the
agenda.
